channel.title: Daily Maverick - Latest News
channel.description: Latest news and analysis from Daily Maverick

item.title: AFTER THE BELL: Why are SA’s cannabis rules still up in smoke?
item.description: Eight years after a court ruling, South Africa still lacks workable cannabis rules, frustrating consumers, businesses and efforts to bring the industry into the formal economy.
item.author: Stephen Grootes

item.title: GEOPOLITICS OP-ED: Brazil’s election — a victory for Lula, a wake-up call for democracy
item.description: Lula’s narrow victory matters far beyond Brazil. It represents Brazil’s place in a fractured world while questioning whether the country can finally convert extraordinary potential into prosperity. But the message from voters and a right-leaning legislature is clear: political history and ideological loyalties are no substitute for delivery.
item.author: Lyal White

item.title: OBITUARY: Paris Mashile — regulator who fought to make SA’s phone calls cheaper
item.description: The engineer, political activist and Shakespeare lover turned the technical machinery of communications into a public argument about power, access and accountability.
item.author: Herman Lategan

item.title: Watch – The pipeline between US white supremacists and the SA right
item.author: Rebecca Davis

item.title: THE FINANCIAL WELLNESS COACH: Interest on your money in the bank may deliver less than expected after tax
item.description: It’s worth exploring investment options, offshore endowments and estate planning to reduce costs and avoid a hefty SA Revenue Service bill.
item.author: Kenny Meiring

item.title: What it takes to fight increasingly sophisticated, AI-powered disinformation campaigns
item.description: Veteran defender of fact-based journalism and founder of the BBC’s Trusted News Initiative, Jessica Cecil, recently launched a new publication about disinformation. These are her reflections on Athena’s first month in the trenches of the information war.
item.author: Jessica Cecil

item.title: SPY TRIAL : EFF secures Zuma-era SSA spy records as Idac stands by R12m case
item.description: More than a decade after the State Security Agency (SSA) allegedly infiltrated its ranks, the EFF has secured access to court records detailing how the party was targeted and infiltrated. This comes as the two men accused in the R12-million Project Mayibuye case prepare to ask the court to discharge them without presenting a defence.
item.author: Nonkululeko Njilo

item.title: HOSTING AMBITIONS: SA unveils Durban as candidate city in its bid to host the Olympic Games
item.description: The South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee has identified Durban as its preferred host city in its bid to host the 2036 or 2040 Olympic Games. But questions remain about the country’s readiness.
item.author: Annemieke Thomaidis

item.title: POLITICALLY AWEH: Six parties share how they’ll tackle the cost of living
item.description: In episode two of Politically Aweh’s Elections Showdown mini-series, we ask six political party representatives about the cost of living – including transportation costs, electricity tariffs, and municipal rates.
item.author: Politically Aweh

item.title: El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti for rescue while elections postponed
item.description: El Salvador will send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to rescue missing personnel and support anti-gang security operations, its foreign ministry said on Wednesday, while Haiti's electoral council postponed planned presidential elections to next year.
item.author: Reuters

item.title: Taiwan flags ‘obvious’ threat from 50 Chinese vessels in wide sweep of waters
item.description: China has more than 50 navy and other official vessels operating in a wide swath of sea stretching from southern Japan down to Taiwan and off the Philippines, a senior Taiwan official said, calling the threat level "obvious"
item.author: Reuters

item.title: North Korea fires around 10 ballistic missiles toward sea off east coast, Seoul says
item.description: North Korea fired around 10 ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast on Thursday, South Korea's military said, as tensions run high ahead of Pyongyang's end-of-month deadline to activate propaganda loudspeakers along the heavily armed border.
item.author: Reuters

item.title: ANALYSIS: So you want to govern a metro? Be careful what you wish for
item.description: The Electoral Commission says 546 parties are contesting these elections, claiming to want to be part of governing our councils and metros. They should think very carefully about that.
item.author: Stephen Grootes

item.title: HOUSEHOLD SQUEEZE: Fuel levy cut offers brief relief as food basket outpaces SA’s unchanged SRD grant
item.description: High fuel prices are squeezing South African household budgets, while the R370 Social Relief of Distress grant still falls short of the cost of a basic food basket.
item.author: Iman Allie

item.title: WHAT’S COOKING: Rich, fruity Christmas cake
item.description: Fruit, nuts, spices and strong liquor — that’s the recipe for the kind of traditional Christmas cake that is made two months in advance. This is the one we made a year ago, and now is the best time to get yours made. It’s best to make a family occasion of it, creating memories along with a cake to look forward to.
item.author: Tony Jackman

item.title: BOOK EXCERPT: Sandstone Estates – where steam locomotives bring SA railway history to life
item.description: Trains, planes, automobiles, tanks and tractors will all gather at Sandstone Estates in the Eastern Free State in mid-November to celebrate the magic of old machines and cherries.
item.author: Chris Marais

item.title: AMABHUNGANE: Takeover row: Butters vs the Takeover Regulation Panel — and Warren Chapman
item.description: The Takeover Regulation Panel is supposed to protect minority shareholders. Did it fold under pressure when confronting broker Peresec and its powerful boss Warren Chapman? Activist shareholder Craig Butters is making that claim in a high-stakes court case.
item.author: Dewald van Rensburg and Sam Sole for amaBhungane

item.title: Alphabet stock sinks as search woes cause revenue miss, cash burn worsens
item.description: Oct 28 (Reuters) - Google parent Alphabet reported disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn as it poured resources into building out AI.
item.author: Reuters

item.title: Leak website releases data on thousands of US Homeland Security employees
item.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 28 (Reuters) - The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.
item.author: Reuters

item.title: Judge rejects US Justice Dept bid to block votes from alleged noncitizens in California
item.description: Oct 28 (Reuters) - A US judge strongly rebuked the Trump administration on Wednesday by rejecting a request by the Justice Department to temporarily block California from counting mail ballots for the midterm elections from more than 20,000 registered voters the department alleges are likely noncitizens.
item.author: Reuters

item.title: After landing in US, Flavio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil’s rightful leader
item.description: SAO PAULO, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Senator Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself Brazil's rightful leader on Wednesday after arriving in the United States, alleging he was the victim of an electoral coup by the country's Supreme Court and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who won the vote by over 4 million votes.
item.author: Reuters

item.title: ANALYSIS: Treasury faces high-stakes battle on the road to social safety net grant reform
item.description: South Africa operates one of the largest social assistance systems in the developing world. The broader social wage – including spending on education, healthcare and other social services – accounts for over 60% of government expenditure. Of course there will be resistance to any change.
item.author: Lindsey Schutters

item.title: PROJECT MAYIBUYE: SSA operation targeting EFF lacked national security basis, court told
item.description: Project Mayibuye should have been stopped before it started. Instead, the Gauteng High Court heard, the secret State Security Agency operation went ahead, targeted the EFF and had millions channelled through it.
item.author: Nonkululeko Njilo

item.title: STING OPERATION: SA ‘refugee’ in US faces decades behind bars on child sexual exploitation charges
item.description: The American Dream of ‘refugee’ Arno Venter has come crashing down after just four months with his arrest and indictment on 11 charges involving child sexual abuse material.
item.author: Rebecca Davis

item.title: Watch — Frank Chikane, DA polls and the ANC’s retreat from the cities
item.author: Mondli Makhanya and Ferial Haffajee

item.title: XENOBAROMETER: Ugandan man nearly killed by March and March mob speaks from hospital
item.description: ‘Simon’, recovering in hospital after a Durban mob attack, recounts fleeing masked protesters and losing consciousness as concerns grow over anti-immigrant violence in 2026.
item.author: Riley Singh

item.title: TRC Roulette : Apartheid’s scapegoat — the jarring paradox of mass killer Eugene de Kock
item.description: Testifying at the Khampepe Inquiry, the former Vlakplaas commander lays bare how political interference and a ‘rotten system’ shielded the generals while leaving him to take the fall alone.
item.author: Marianne Thamm

item.title: CRIMEFIGHTING REFORM: R1bn in recovered loot to fund Firoz Cachalia’s police reset
item.description: Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia says money taken from criminals is funding the fight against organised crime, while broad reforms are under way to depoliticise the police, rebuild Crime Intelligence and clean up SAPS procurement processes.
item.author: Ferial Haffajee

item.title: GOVERNANCE FIASCO OP-ED: Bronkhorstspruit gastro outbreak: A failure to keep people safe
item.description: With 833 people seeking treatment, Bronkhorstspruit’s outbreak highlights how failures in water treatment and government leadership put vulnerable communities at risk.
item.author: The Independent Science Reference Group

item.title: Yawn-fest — political parties bore voters with dull election slogans, poles show
item.description: Voters are being bored to death by pathetic political party slogans and posters as we head for the seminal 4 November local government elections.
item.author: Peter Mann

item.title: DOUBLE TROUBLE: Suliman Carrim granted R100K bail in Madlanga case, but remains jailed on car-smuggling charges
item.description: North West businessman Suliman Carrim was granted bail for failing to continue testifying at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry. However, he remains behind bars on separate car-smuggling charges, in a case where two of his co-accused may plead guilty.
item.author: Caryn Dolley

item.title: Markets are waking up to the risks they have spent months ignoring
item.description: Markets are showing signs of a major shift as concerns over inflated AI valuations, economic growth and interest rates drive investors away from equities and towards government bonds. Upcoming central bank signals and tech earnings could determine whether markets stabilise or face a deeper sell-off in the months ahead.
item.author: Natale Labia

item.title: As Trump staggers to the polls, Americans yearning for change prepare to say ‘enough’
item.description: It is hard to fully describe the epic destruction Trump has wrought, and next Tuesday the Americans will deliver a verdict on all of it – and it doesn’t look good for him. His name might not be on any ballot on 3 November, but the election is a referendum on his presidency.
item.author: Phillip van Niekerk

item.title: Fuel levy remedy: Relief for a month, pressure for a lifetime
item.description: The 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement offers a welcome pause at the petrol pump, but mistakes temporary relief for a durable answer to South Africa’s cost-of-living crisis.
item.author: Baneng Naape

item.title: Right of reply: SA needs more factories, not more walls
item.description: Chinese electric vehicles and investment can boost South African manufacturing, create jobs and accelerate the affordable green transition, while tariffs risk harming consumers and businesses. South Africa should protect its economic sovereignty and maintain strong trade ties with both China and the European Union.
item.author: Wang Chuan

item.title: Wildlife is not livestock — Aucamp’s dangerous plan to turn conservation into agriculture
item.description: Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp wants South Africa’s wildlife ranching industry transferred to his department. Behind the rhetoric of economic growth and sustainable use lies a potentially far-reaching attempt to redefine wildlife as an agricultural commodity, raising serious constitutional, ecological and ethical questions.
item.author: Adam Cruise

item.title: There is another Afrikaner story worth telling, rooted in reconciliation and a shared future
item.description: While much of the international discussion about Afrikaners focuses on fear and persecution, there are people whose lives tell a different story about our place in South Africa.
item.author: Deon Snyman

item.title: Mantashe shifts focus from women’s vulnerability to linguistic legitimacy
item.description: The debate around Mineral and Petroleum Resources Minister Gwede Mantashe’s remarks about women seeking job opportunities being asked for sexual favours by men occupying positions of authority has turned into a discussion about language, and obscures the original question put to him concerning allegations of exploitation and power.
item.author: Naledi Maponopono-Manopi

item.title: The other Pillay at the Geneva pharmacy
item.description: A surname coincidence in Switzerland brings back memories of my parents’ generation, and the opportunities opened to some women and denied to others.
item.author: Ravi Pillay

item.title: East African Crude Oil Pipeline financing: Can Standard Bank’s climate claims survive scrutiny
item.description: Standard Bank cannot market itself as a champion of human rights and green progress while it bankrolls environmental destruction and community dispossession in east Africa. This matter is now before South Africa’s Advertising Regulatory Board.
item.author: Flevian Bonareri Machoka and Kholwani Simelane

item.title: Regulation of religion — SA must tackle religious abuse without restricting freedom of belief
item.description: On International Religious Freedom Day, the biggest threat facing religious freedom in SA is an institution created to protect it.
item.author: Craig Bailie

item.title: Dealing with conservation’s inconvenient individual
item.description: Conservation may save species, but what does it cost individual animals? Welfare belongs in the ethical calculus: sustainable is not always ethically justified.
item.author: Dave Morgan

item.title: Local elections 2026: How do you choose who to vote for?
item.description: Local elections are about more than party loyalty: scrutinise candidates, understand the job and decide what accountability should look like five years from now.
item.author: Mbali Ntuli

item.title: Why the best-laid plans to fix Joburg won’t work — and what will
item.description: Fixing our municipalities requires more than listing obvious infrastructural failures. True recovery demands structural debt relief, national-level support and clear operational strategies to allow incoming leadership a fresh starting point to rebuild.
item.author: Mark Barnes

item.title: When the state fails to protect you, self-defence isn’t a luxury; it’s a necessity
item.description: Amid a failure of state protection, disarming law-abiding citizens through the Firearms Control Amendment Bill and ignoring the Private Security Industry Regulatory Authority’s governance crisis will fuel chaos rather than safety.
item.author: Ian Cameron

item.title: El Niño threatens to deepen southern Africa’s poverty crisis
item.description: An expected El Niño drought, rising costs and shrinking humanitarian aid could worsen food insecurity and poverty across southern Africa in 2027. South Africa’s strong grain harvest and water reserves offer some protection, but regional food shortages may increase pressure on supplies and exports.
item.author: Wandile Sihlobo

item.title: Lula’s Brazil election win has given the world breathing space
item.description: Lula da Silva’s historic fourth-term victory in Brazil signals hope for multilateralism, climate action and the Global South. With profound geopolitical implications for global sovereignty, it also presents a crucial opportunity for South Africa.
item.author: Redi Tlhabi

item.title: Watch – Top Court puts ANC candidates back on ballot after missed deadline
item.author: Lerato Mutsila and Tamsin Metelerkamp

item.title: Watch - Ramaphosa’s reform message as polls show continued ANC decline
item.author: Ferial Haffajee and Mondli Makhanya

item.title: Watch – Ferial Haffajee and Ernst Roets on Agoa, crosses and autonomy
item.author: Ferial Haffajee
